Palantir Alumni’s Onodrim Raises $300 Million to Buy Up Europe’s Defense Suppliers
Jakob Steinschaden , co-produced by AI 09. November 2026, 09:06
Onodrim Industries raised $300 million in a Series A round. © Fred Hayes / Getty Images for Onodrim Industries
Set Trending Topics as a preferred source on Google.
Europe has a new defense unicorn, and it doesn’t build a single drone itself: Onodrim Industries, based in Amsterdam, has closed a $300 million Series A round. The company is now valued at $1.3 billion. Founded by former Palantir employees, it plans to use the money to take majority stakes in established suppliers to the defense, aerospace and manufacturing industries.
The Year’s Largest Series A
The round was led by Lux Capital, an early backer of Anduril, according to the company’s press release . New and existing investors including General Catalyst, Lakestar, Altimeter, Strike Capital, 137 Ventures, 8090 and Expeditions also took part. Onodrim says it is the largest European Series A of 2026. The company raised more than $45 million earlier this year.
The round ended up considerably larger than first planned. In late September, Bloomberg reported that Onodrim was seeking about 200 million euros at a $1 billion valuation.
Buy, Digitize, Scale
The business model looks more like private equity than a typical start-up. Onodrim plans to invest in manufacturers whose products have both civilian and military uses and that sit in the defense industry’s supply chains, where bottlenecks are currently common. The acquired companies are to receive long-term capital along with software and Onodrim’s own engineering teams, who will digitize production and develop new products so the companies can take on larger defense contracts.
Europe has many outstanding companies, but they often lack the resources to grow as fast as is now needed, said Aistis Šimaitis, Onodrim’s co-founder and chief executive. The company plans to announce its first acquisitions in the coming months. Its co-founder Alex Blessing is directly inviting owners of defense, aerospace and industrial businesses to get in touch.
Palantir DNA and an Office in Munich
Mr. Šimaitis previously advised the Lithuanian government, held a senior technology role at Palantir Technologies and earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. Alexander Blessing, the chief technology officer, studied at Stanford and Cambridge and worked at Palantir as a forward deployed engineer, embedded directly with customers. The founding team also includes Christian Garrett, a partner at 137 Ventures. In addition to Amsterdam, London and Vilnius, Onodrim is now opening offices in Munich and Turin.
Investors are betting on the model. Europe needs a stronger industrial foundation to meet the security challenges ahead, said Brandon Reeves, a partner at Lux Capital. Jeannette zu Fürstenberg, president of General Catalyst, sees Onodrim as redefining the industrial conglomerate: Europe’s established manufacturers already have the expertise, customers and trust, she said, but they lack cutting-edge technology.
The Competition
Onodrim is entering a booming market. European defense tech companies are raising billions, led by Munich-based Helsing, which recently raised $1.8 billion at an $18 billion valuation , and Quantum Systems. The Institutional Infrastructure Battery Fund (IIBF) is launching as an infrastructure investment fund for institutional investors, specifically focused on large-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Germany. At launch, the fund has already secured its first two storage projects in central Germany under purchase agreements and has an identified project pipeline representing an investment volume of more than €300 million.
As renewable energy deployment progresses, large-scale battery storage systems are becoming an important component in stabilizing the German electricity grid and balancing volatile generation peaks. The IIBF translates this structural infrastructure need into an investment profile tailored to regulated institutional investors: the fund invests in a diversified portfolio of large-scale battery storage projects in Germany that are ready to build or close to their commercial operation date (COD) and holds them for the long term following acquisition. Early-stage project development and permitting risks therefore remain outside the fund.
Clearly defined responsibilities: institutional investment management and European energy trading expertise
The IIBF is built on a clearly defined division of responsibilities between two established specialists in their respective markets:
Investment management, underwriting and structuring by 2IP: Institutional Investment Partners (2IP) is responsible for investment management, transaction underwriting and institutional fund structuring. As the storage facilities are held throughout the fund's term, pre-acquisition due diligence is particularly important: 2IP assesses each transaction against clearly defined risk, financial viability and cash flow criteria, incorporates contractual security mechanisms and provides ongoing oversight through its portfolio and investment management.
Market access, asset management, software and energy trading by Second Foundation: As one of Europe's major technology-driven energy traders, the Second Foundation Group manages the energy-related and technological value chain surrounding the storage facilities. This ranges from direct project access and commercial and technical asset management of the facilities, through proprietary control and monitoring software, to high-frequency trading of capacity in the European electricity and balancing markets.
Contractually underpinned base distributions with additional market upside
The IIBF's income model is designed to cushion downside exposure to the volatility typical of electricity markets while also harnessing it for the portfolio. The core of the fund's income consists of long-term contractual usage fees (lease payments) for making the storage facilities available. Contractual advance payments and additional security mechanisms support the predictability of regular distributions to investors.

articles.text:
AI agents are moving out of experiments and into day-to-day work, and building, running and watching them has become a new problem for companies. Picking a model is not enough. Teams need to trace why an agent got something wrong, catch performance slipping in production, and control which tools and data it can reach. LangChain , whose platform targets exactly that, has raised $300 million in a Series C.
From open-source framework to agent engineering platform
LangChain says its mission is to help every company own its intelligence. As agents transform the economy, it says, companies are building domain-specific agents differentiated by their knowledge, data and user experience, and the companies that control them will gain lasting advantages.
The product centers on LangSmith and rests on three pillars. Agent Runtime covers running agents reliably. Deep Agents, LangGraph and LangChain give developers flexibility across models and control over context. LangSmith Agent Server and Sandboxes deploy agents securely at scale in the cloud or a customer’s own environment, and Managed Agents and Fleet run mission-critical agents as managed services. Agent Improvement covers testing and monitoring. Observability and Evaluation show how agents behave and measure quality, and LangSmith Engine, an in-platform agent, finds errors, writes code and prompt fixes and watches production traffic for regressions. Fine-Tuning turns traces into training data for specialized models. Agent Governance gives central control over models, tools and data. LLM and Tool Gateways manage model budgets and fallbacks, protect sensitive data, and govern tool access and authentication.
More than 7,000 organizations already use LangSmith, according to LangChain, from fast-growing startups such as Harvey , Rippling and Listen Labs to Fortune 500 enterprises such as Nvidia , Toyota and Salesforce . Clay uses it to monitor hundreds of millions of agent runs a month. Workday uses it to run and govern agents across the organization, cutting the time to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day. These figures come from the company and have not been independently verified.
A side project that started weeks after ChatGPT
LangChain began within weeks of ChatGPT’s release in late 2022. Harrison Chase , then an engineer at Robust Intelligence, started it as a personal open-source project to fix a gap in large language models: they could not reach live information or take real actions such as web search or API calls. After founding the company with Ankush Gola, he raised a $10 million seed led by Benchmark in April 2023 and a $25 million Series A led by Sequoia in February 2024, at a $200 million valuation.
Valuation more than doubles in a year
LangChain said on Nov. 13 that it raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $460 million. Existing investor CapitalG led, with significant participation from new investors GIC and DFJ Growth and existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures .
New investors also include Salesforce Ventures , Insight Partners , QuantumLight and MongoDB Ventures, and existing investors Sequoia , Amplify and Benchmark returned. LangChain became a unicorn last October with a $125 million Series B at a $1.25 billion valuation, so its valuation has more than doubled in about a year.

LangChain Raises $300 Million Series C at $3 Billion Valuation to Advance Enterprise AI Agents
By Ash Kate November 14, 2026
Article content
LangChain Secures $300 Million to Advance Enterprise AI Agents
LangChain has raised $300 million in a Series C funding round at a $3 billion valuation, strengthening its position in the rapidly expanding enterprise AI agent market. The round was led by existing investor CapitalG , with significant participation from new investors GIC and DFJ Growth, alongside existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures.
The latest funding brings LangChain's total capital raised to approximately $460 million. The investment comes as businesses increasingly explore AI agents to automate workflows, develop intelligent applications and transform internal operations.
The company plans to use the funding to advance its mission of enabling every organisation to own its intelligence, with a focus on giving businesses greater control over the models, data and infrastructure powering their AI systems.
Expanding LangSmith's Enterprise AI Capabilities
At the centre of LangChain's strategy is LangSmith, its framework-agnostic platform designed to help organisations run, improve and govern AI agents.
The company reports that more than 7,000 organisations already rely on LangSmith, spanning fast-growing technology companies and large enterprises. Its customers include Harvey, Rippling and Listen Labs, alongside NVIDIA, Toyota and Salesforce.
LangChain is developing its platform around three core capabilities: Agent Runtime, Agent Improvement and Agent Governance.
Agent Runtime provides the infrastructure and tools required to build, deploy and operate agents reliably. Agent Improvement focuses on observability, evaluation and continuous performance optimisation, while Agent Governance gives organisations greater control over model usage, data protection, tool access and authentication.
These capabilities address some of the operational challenges businesses encounter when moving AI agents from experimentation into production environments.
Building Greater Control Over Enterprise Intelligence
LangChain's funding announcement reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI adoption, where the focus is moving beyond building AI-powered applications towards managing intelligent systems at scale.
The company believes domain-specific agents, differentiated by their knowledge, data and user experience, will play an increasingly important role in both standalone software products and internal business operations.
Its approach centres on giving organisations the flexibility to choose models, maintain control over their data and infrastructure, and continuously improve their agents without being restricted to a single model ecosystem.
LangChain also highlighted customer deployments that demonstrate the platform's enterprise applications. According to the company, Clay uses LangSmith to monitor hundreds of millions of agent runs each month, while Workday has reduced the time required to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day.

Q-CTRL: $290 Million Series C Funding Led By Salesforce Ventures Creates New Quantum Technology Unicorn
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 14, 2026
Q-CTRL: $290 Million Series C Funding Led By Salesforce Ventures Creates New Quantum Technology Unicorn
Q-CTRL, a developer of AI-powered quantum infrastructure software, has raised $290 million (A$415 million) in Series C funding led by Salesforce Ventures, with significant participation from Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners. The oversubscribed financing establishes Q-CTRL as a new quantum technology unicorn and provides capital to accelerate the commercialization of its quantum computing and sensing technologies across data centers, aviation, autonomous systems, and other industries.
The Series C round was expanded twice to accommodate investor demand and represents what the company describes as the largest fundraising round for a software-focused business in the quantum sector.
The investment will support Q-CTRL’s global expansion, continued development of its AI-powered quantum infrastructure platform, and commercialization of technologies designed to make quantum systems more reliable in real-world environments.
New investors include Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners, Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation, and SPARX Asset Management.
Returning investors include Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures, and Square Peg.
The investor group brings together venture capital firms, strategic corporate investors, and institutions with experience across AI, aerospace, defense, semiconductors, and industrial technologies.
Combining Artificial Intelligence And Quantum Computing
Q-CTRL develops infrastructure software designed to improve the performance and reliability of quantum technologies.
Its platform uses AI-powered control techniques to address technical challenges that have historically limited the practical application of quantum computing and quantum sensing.
Quantum systems are highly sensitive to environmental interference, noise, and other sources of error.
These challenges can reduce the accuracy and reliability of quantum operations, making it difficult to achieve useful results outside carefully controlled laboratory environments.
Q-CTRL’s software is designed to mitigate these limitations through techniques that improve how quantum hardware operates.
The company takes a hardware-agnostic approach, allowing its technologies to work across different quantum computing and sensing platforms.
According to Q-CTRL, its software can increase the effective computational capabilities of quantum machines by thousands of times in certain applications.
The company’s strategy focuses on making existing and emerging quantum hardware more useful rather than developing competing quantum processors.
This approach positions Q-CTRL as a provider of infrastructure software that could support multiple participants across the quantum technology industry.
Salesforce Ventures Leads Major Quantum Investment
Salesforce Ventures led the financing based on Q-CTRL’s progress in turning quantum technology into practical commercial applications.
Robert Keith, Partner at Salesforce Ventures, highlighted the importance of software in enabling quantum computers to produce reliable, useful results.

articles.text:
Money is pouring into companies that build quantum computers. Oratomic raised a $475 million Series B in October, and Universal Quantum closed a Series A of more than $100 million. But whether qubits are made from neutral atoms or trapped ions, the problem is the same: they are sensitive to noise and make errors mid-calculation. Q-CTRL , an Australian company that sells software to reduce those errors, said it raised a $290 million Series C (A$415 million). It says the round makes it the newest quantum unicorn, though it did not disclose a valuation.
Software that makes other companies’ chips usable
Q-CTRL does not build quantum computers. Founded in 2017 by Michael Biercuk , a University of Sydney physicist, it sells software that helps machines built by other companies run better. It pitches a hardware-agnostic design that is not tied to any one qubit technology.
It has two main products. Fire Opal is cloud software that automatically shortens the quantum circuits a developer writes, maps them onto a chip according to each machine’s error profile and corrects measurement errors before returning results. It runs on IBM’s quantum service, IonQ and Rigetti systems and Amazon Braket, among others, and the company claims it can run circuits up to 10 times deeper on the same hardware. Boulder Opal is for those who build or operate quantum computers. Even after it is switched on, a quantum computer needs its control signals tuned qubit by qubit, and the product automates that calibration and upkeep without a team of physicists. It supports superconducting and semiconductor spin-qubit machines, with trapped-ion and neutral-atom support available on request, the company says. Its target customers are chipmakers and data center and HPC operators. In computing, the company also claims a 3,000x speedup in materials discovery for the energy sector.
The third business pairs software with sensors. Ironstone Opal is a navigation system for places where GPS is unavailable or jammed. It measures tiny variations in the Earth’s magnetic field and matches them against a magnetic map to find its position. The company builds the quantum magnetometers itself, and AI software filters out the magnetic interference the aircraft generates. The company says the system is 100 times better than the best alternative, but in its published flight trial it reported up to 50 times lower positioning uncertainty than an inertial navigation system. It says Ironstone Opal is being deployed on commercial aircraft with Airbus, on autonomous platforms with Lockheed Martin and on drones. All performance figures come from the company.
Led by Salesforce Ventures, expanded twice
Salesforce Ventures led the round, with Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners named as headline participants. The company says it expanded the round twice to meet investor demand and calls it the largest raise by a software-focused quantum company. Q-CTRL expanded its Series B to $113 million in October 2024.

Returning investors are Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures and Square Peg. Q-CTRL raises $290 million in Series C funding round with participation from UAE’s EDGE
Published on: 16 November، 2026
Q-CTRL, a company specializing in quantum technology infrastructure software development, has raised $290 million in a Series C investment round, with the participation of the UAE's EDGE Group, which injected $50 million into the company.
Q-CTRL, a company specializing in quantum technology infrastructure software development, has raised $290 million in a Series C investment round, with the participation of the UAE’s EDGE Group, which injected $50 million into the company.
Headquartered in Sydney, Q-CTRL develops software solutions for quantum technology applications, including quantum navigation systems designed to operate in environments where satellite navigation services are unavailable or unreliable, applications aimed at supporting autonomous platforms and unmanned vehicles.
EDGE joined a new group of investors in the funding round , which included strategic companies, private equity investors, and investors specializing in growth-stage corporate financing.
Rodrigo Torres, Chief Financial Officer of EDGE Group, stated that the investment gives the group a direct presence in one of the fields of advanced technology, pointing out that quantum technology is moving at an accelerated pace from laboratories to practical applications.
He added that EDGE is working in parallel to develop technological capabilities, acquire them, build partnerships, and invest in them, enabling the group to keep pace with technologies that will shape future capabilities.
The investment comes as part of EDGE’s orientation to enhance its capabilities in the fields of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and navigation technologies capable of operating in environments lacking traditional navigation services.
The group recently integrated autonomous systems within a maritime demonstration carried out by the UAE Navy with the participation of allied forces, which included the operation of surface drone vessels, anti-drone systems, and anti-jamming technologies within a coordinated mission.

Salesforce stock: Salesforce Ventures leads US$290 million Q-CTRL round
Published on 11/16/2026 at 17:11 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS
Salesforce stock is in focus after Salesforce Ventures led Q-CTRL's US$290 million round. The November 12 financing targets quantum software and GPS-free navigation.
Q-CTRL round broadens Salesforce's AI reach
Salesforce Ventures led an oversubscribed US$290 million Series C round for Q-CTRL on November 12.
Q-CTRL plans to scale its quantum software and navigation business globally across finance, energy, autonomy and aerospace.
Salesforce, US79466L3024, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Salesforce Ventures led a US$290 million Series C funding round for quantum infrastructure software company Q-CTRL on November 12. The oversubscribed financing gives Salesforce's venture operation a prominent role in a private quantum technology investment and adds a new strategic angle ahead of Salesforce's next results.
Q-CTRL announced the financing in its Q-CTRL announcement . The company said the round reached US$290 million, equivalent to A$415 million, after two expansions to meet investor demand. Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners made significant contributions, while other new and returning investors included AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, In-Q-Tel and Lockheed Martin Ventures.
Quantum software becomes the focus
Q-CTRL said it will use the new capital to strengthen its software-first strategy and expand globally. Its products target quantum computing and sensing, including Ironstone Opal, a navigation system designed for use when GPS is unavailable or denied.
Robert Keith, a Salesforce Ventures partner, said Q-CTRL's AI-powered control software addresses the challenge of turning quantum hardware output into useful results. For Salesforce, the investment broadens exposure to a technology layer that could support enterprise computing, autonomy and aerospace applications, although Q-CTRL remains a private company outside Salesforce's core operating segments.
Salesforce stock traded at 197.91 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:05 CET on Monday, November 16, 2026.
